mainTopic: Do רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי accept ברירה? עולא's reading of the wine ברייתא, and רבי יוסי's ruling on the women's bird offerings (קינים)
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא about a person who buys untithed wine from כותים. רבי מאיר lets him declare now that the portions he will separate later are already תרומה and מעשרות, and then drink right away. That only works through ברירה, and רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it. This seems to support איו's teaching that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, which clashes with our משנה. עולא sides with the משנה and rejects איו. To explain the ברייתא, he groups the names in pairs, so רבי יהודה joins רבי מאיר and only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid. The גמרא then asks whether רבי יוסי really rejects ברירה, because in a משנה about two women's bird offerings (קינים) he lets the כהן decide which bird is an עולה and which a חטאת. רבה answers that the women made an explicit stipulation. The גמרא shows the משנה still teaches something new: the rule of רב חסדא about when bird offerings get their identity, a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The wine-from-כותים ברייתא: רבי מאיר permits, three תנאים forbid
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא. רבי מאיר lets a person designate future portions of wine as תרומה and מעשרות and drink at once. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid this, which seems to show they reject ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: 'The two לוגין that I will separate later are תרומה. Ten are מעשר ראשון. Nine are מעשר שני.' He redeems the מעשר שני with money and drinks right away. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about drinking untithed wine by designating, in advance, the portions that will be separated later. רבי מאיר allows it, but three other תנאים, including רבי יהודה, forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's leniency only works with ברירה: the wine left at the end is treated as if it had always been the תרומה and מעשרות. Those who forbid seem to reject ברירה. Since רבי יהודה is on the forbidding list, this ברייתא appears to back איו, who taught that רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה. That clashes with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure; the case involves a 100-לוג barrel
The portion of produce given to a כהן
First tithe, given to a לוי
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed with money
He redeems (here, the מעשר שני with money)
They forbid

steps.confusionAlert: Nothing is physically separated before he drinks. He only names the amounts now. The actual wine set aside at the end is 'clarified' as having been the תרומה all along. That idea is ברירה.

phrases.english: He says: two log
phrases.notes: This continues a ברייתא about someone who buys wine from כותים on ערב שבת.

phrases.english: which I will separate in the future
phrases.notes: He means out of the 100 לוג, and he'll actually separate them only after he's done drinking.

phrases.english: are hereby teruma,
ten are first tithe,
nine are second tithe,
phrases.notes: That's a tenth of the remaining ninety.

phrases.english: and he redeems [the second tithe] and drinks immediately —
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
and Rabbi Shimon forbid it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אומר: שני לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש הרי הן תרומה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun earlier. It is cited as evidence that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, supporting איו against our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds אין ברירה (as איו taught)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of wine bought from כותים, where רבי יהודה is listed among those who forbid

steps.title: עולא rejects איו's teaching because of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that איו's report of רבי יהודה is not accepted, because it contradicts our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: איו's teaching is not valid, because of our משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא takes the opposite side. He trusts the משנה, where רבי יהודה accepts ברירה, and throws out איו's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have two clashing reports of רבי יהודה: the משנה (he accepts ברירה) and איו (he rejects it). עולא decides the clash in favor of the משנה. That leaves him needing an answer for the ברייתא just quoted, which seemed to support איו.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not; it is rejected
A תנא who taught that רבי יהודה rejects ברירה
Our משנה

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Ayo's [teaching] is rejected because of our Mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the opposite resolution: the משנה wins and איו is rejected, despite the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איו's teaching is set aside; רבי יהודה accepts ברירה, as the משנה shows.

steps.title: But the ברייתא lists רבי יהודה among those who forbid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges עולא: the ברייתא clearly lists רבי יהודה with those who forbid, which implies he rejects ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what the ברייתא teaches: 'רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on עולא. If רבי יהודה accepts ברירה, why does the ברייתא count him among those who forbid relying on it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if איו can be dismissed, the ברייתא is an independent source showing רבי יהודה rejects ברירה. עולא's position is under attack until he explains this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But then (what about...)
That which is taught

phrases.english: But then, that which is taught:
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
and Rabbi Shimon forbid — [what about that?]

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling from step 2, using the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that רבי יהודה accepts ברירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists רבי יהודה among those who forbid, which only makes sense if he holds אין ברירה.

steps.title: עולא reads the names in pairs: רבי יהודה joins רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: עולא regroups the names in the ברייתא into pairs. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה permit, while רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא teaches the names in pairs: 'These are the words of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. He reads the ברייתא differently, so that רבי יהודה stands with רבי מאיר on the permitting side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this regrouping, רבי יהודה accepts ברירה in the ברייתא too, matching the משנה. The forbidding side now has only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון. This sets up the next question about רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: In pairs; two by two

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not inventing a new opinion. He is changing how the list of names is grouped, so רבי יהודה moves from the forbidding group to the permitting group.
steps.whatToRemember: According to עולא, רבי יהודה accepts ברירה, both in the משנה and in the ברייתא. Only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid in the wine case.

phrases.english: Ulla teaches [the names] in pairs:
these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by re-dividing the names in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the text (regrouping the list of names)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה was grouped with רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון as forbidding, so he rejects ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה is paired with רבי מאיר as permitting. Only רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון forbid.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי reject ברירה? The two women's bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי rejects ברירה. In a משנה about two women's mixed bird offerings, he lets the כהן decide which bird is an עולה and which a חטאת, which seems to be ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold אין ברירה? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי says, if two women bought their pairs of birds together, or gave their birds to the כהן, the כהן may offer whichever he wants as an עולה and whichever he wants as a חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that רבי יוסי is clearly on the forbidding side, the גמרא challenges that position. A משנה shows רבי יוסי letting a later choice decide which bird belongs to which offering, and that sounds like ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman after childbirth brings two birds: one עולה and one חטאת. When the birds were bought together without specifying, letting the כהן choose later means the choice 'clarifies' what each bird was all along. That is exactly ברירה, so רבי יוסי's ruling here seems to contradict his forbidding in the wine ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no retroactive designation
Pairs of bird offerings (turtledoves or pigeons)
Jointly, mixed together without specifying
Burnt offering
Sin offering

steps.confusionAlert: Here בעירוב does not mean an עירוב תחומין. It simply means 'mixed together / jointly purchased.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא now has to work out רבי יוסי's real position on ברירה. The answer will shape how we understand the dispute over conditional עירובין.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold there is no retroactive designation?
But didn't we learn in a Mishna: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֶׁלָּקְחוּ אֶת קִינֵּיהֶן בְּעֵירוּב,
phrases.english: two women who bought their bird pairs jointly,
or who gave their bird pairs to the priest —
phrases.notes: Without saying which bird is for which offering

phrases.english: whichever the priest wants, he may offer as a burnt offering,
and whichever he wants, he may offer as a sin offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: וסבר רבי יוסי אין ברירה? והתנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up the result of step 4 (רבי יוסי forbids, implying אין ברירה) and challenges it with a contradicting משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רבי יוסי holds אין ברירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the קינים משנה, רבי יוסי lets the כהן's later choice determine which bird was each offering. That is retroactive designation, so he seems to accept ברירה.

steps.title: רבה: In the bird case the women made a stipulation
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers the challenge from רבי יוסי's ruling on the birds. In that case the women explicitly agreed in advance that the כהן would decide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: There, it is a case where they made a stipulation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends the claim that רבי יוסי rejects ברירה. He explains that the bird case is a special situation, not real ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברירה means that a later choice reveals what was meant from the start. In the bird case, the women said openly at the beginning that the כהן would decide. The כהן is simply carrying out their agreed plan, so the case proves nothing about ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in that other משנה
They stipulated, made an explicit condition (from תְּנַאי)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה is saying רבי יוסי accepts ברירה. He is saying the opposite: the bird case works only because of an explicit condition, so it says nothing about ברירה.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
There, it is a case where they stipulated.
phrases.notes: The women agreed from the start to let the priest decide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by narrowing the bird case to one with an explicit stipulation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the source is set in a special situation where the women stipulated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's later choice seemed to be ברירה, which would mean רבי יוסי accepts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The women stipulated in advance, so the כהן just carries out their condition. No ברירה is involved.

steps.title: If they stipulated, why would the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer. If the women made a clear condition, the result is obvious, so why does the משנה bother to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבה's reading. If there was an explicit stipulation, the ruling seems too obvious to need a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is assumed to teach something new. If the women openly agreed that the כהן would decide, of course he may decide. Reading the משנה this way seems to leave it with nothing to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if that is the case
What is there to say? Why state something obvious?

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?
phrases.notes: With an explicit condition, the ruling seems obvious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's limitation from step 6 for making the משנה obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the bird case involved an explicit stipulation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there was a clear condition, the ruling is obvious. A משנה should not teach something obvious, so רבה's reading seems unlikely.

steps.title: The משנה teaches the rule of רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that even with a stipulation, the משנה teaches something new: the rule of רב חסדא about when bird offerings become fixed as עולה or חטאת. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us like רב חסדא. For רב חסדא said: Bird offerings do not become designated [except...].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows what new lesson the משנה contains, which answers the challenge in step 7. It brings in רב חסדא's rule about when bird offerings get their identity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pairs of birds (קינין) do not become a specific עולה or חטאת just by being brought. They are fixed only at certain moments, which the sentence lists on the next amud. The משנה teaches that the birds stay undefined until then, so the כהן is still able to assign them according to the women's condition.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (introduces the new lesson)
Become designated, get their specific identity

steps.whyThisMatters: רב חסדא's rule explains why the כהן can still assign the birds. Until the right moment, they have no fixed identity.

phrases.english: It teaches us in accordance with Rav Chisda,
as Rav Chisda said:
Bird offerings do not become designated [except...]
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which lists the moments when they become designated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7 by showing the new lesson in the משנה, even under רבה's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a hidden new lesson (חידוש) in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With an explicit stipulation, the משנה seemed to teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches רב חסדא's rule that קינין get their identity only at specific moments, so they can still be assigned by the כהן.
